name: Bowel-associated dermatosis-arthritis syndrome
aliases: bowel bypass syndrome without bowel bypass

clinicalPearls: Presents with recurrent crops of small erythematous macules that evolve into papules, vesiculopustules and purpuric lesions, typically on the upper trunk and proximal limbs
The eruption is accompanied by a non-deforming, often migratory polyarthralgia or arthritis and frequently by fever and malaise
It was first described after jejunoileal bypass surgery for obesity but also occurs with inflammatory bowel disease and other conditions causing a blind loop or bacterial overgrowth
The syndrome can arise without any bowel surgery ('bowel bypass syndrome without bowel bypass')
Episodes are recurrent and self-limited, lasting days at a time, and belong to the neutrophilic dermatoses
Biopsy shows a neutrophilic dermal infiltrate resembling early Sweet syndrome, sometimes with leucocytoclasis
Management addresses the underlying bowel abnormality, for example antibiotics for bacterial overgrowth or surgical revision of a bypassed segment
reference.pathophysiology: Bowel-associated dermatosis-arthritis syndrome is thought to arise from bacterial overgrowth within a bypassed, diverticular or diseased segment of bowel. Bacterial antigens, particularly peptidoglycan components, stimulate formation of circulating immune complexes that deposit in the skin and synovium, triggering a neutrophil-rich inflammatory response. This immune-complex-mediated, cross-reactive process produces the recurrent neutrophilic dermatosis and the accompanying arthralgia. The link to intestinal bacterial overgrowth explains why the syndrome responds to measures that reduce the bacterial burden.
additionalDifferentials: Erythema nodosum (as part of inflammatory bowel disease)
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy showing a neutrophilic infiltrate
Evaluation for inflammatory bowel disease or a bypassed/blind bowel loop
Full blood count and inflammatory markers during flares
Blood and, if relevant, joint fluid cultures to exclude sepsis
Imaging or endoscopy of the bowel as indicated
redFlags: Features suggesting septic arthritis or disseminated gonococcal infection requiring urgent exclusion
Systemic sepsis in a patient with a blind bowel loop
Underlying inflammatory bowel disease with complications
reference.prognosis: Individual episodes are self-limited, but without correction of the underlying bowel problem the syndrome tends to recur; treating the intestinal cause, whether by antibiotics or surgical revision, generally controls the disease and carries a good outlook.
pitfalls: Mistaking the eruption and arthritis for a septic process and missing the bowel-related cause
Failing to look for bacterial overgrowth or a bypassed loop in a patient without prior surgery
Treating flares symptomatically while ignoring the underlying gut abnormality
Confusing it with Sweet syndrome without considering the bowel association
management: Antibiotics such as tetracyclines or metronidazole to reduce the intestinal bacterial overgrowth that drives immune-complex formation
Systemic corticosteroids to suppress flares of the neutrophilic dermatosis and accompanying arthralgia
Surgical correction of the underlying blind loop or revision of a jejunoileal bypass when that is the precipitant
Treatment of coexisting inflammatory bowel disease when this is the underlying cause
Symptomatic analgesia for the migratory arthralgia during self-limited episodes
Steroid-sparing agents such as dapsone for frequent or recurrent flares, with monitoring of disease activity
Combined dermatology, gastroenterology and surgical input to address both skin and bowel components
